title: VP incurs P5 million debt from impeach defense, trips
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte says she has incurred a debt of P5 million in 2025 to fund her visits to The Hague, Netherlands where her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, has been detained, and…

blocks.text: November 28, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte says she has incurred a debt of P5 million in 2025 to fund her visits to The Hague, Netherlands where her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, has been detained, and to cover the initial cost of the defense lawyers for her impeachment.
At a press conference yesterday, Duterte said she intends to sell at least two properties to cover her debt.

With her father facing trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC) for allegedly committing crimes against humanity and her impeachment case, the Vice President said, “For me, the most difficult part of the trial is paying the professional fees of the lawyers. I still have a lot of debt. There are a lot of lawyers, I owe many of them.”
“But I am fortunate that I am not part of the legal team of president Duterte anymore so I don’t have to worry about paying the legal fees of his lawyers in the ICC,” she added.

Duterte could not cite an exact figure on how much money she owes, but admitted that she had to borrow P5 million from two friends from Davao City “just to cover the costs of going back and forth to The Hague and dealing with the defense team of president Duterte in the ICC and in preparing for my impeachment case.”
She has not yet paid her debt from last year. “But I intend to sell properties. So, that would cover the debt.”
With Duterte’s impeachment case in full swing, she expects that her expenses in 2026 would be higher than last year.
Meanwhile, she is also hoping the ICC would allow her father to attend the hearing remotely so he would not have to sit for eight hours during the trial.
Duterte said she is not expecting the former leader to get a fair trial, but has no complaints on how he is being treated while in prison.
‘Plastikan’ is nat’l sport of pols
The Vice President was at the Senate on Nov. 26 for deliberations of the Office of the Vice President (OVP)’s budget.
“I was in the Senate yesterday for the OVP budget proposal for the plenary, and we thank the Senate for the approval of the budget for the OVP.”
She said it was a “pleasant” experience.
However, during her small talk with some senators, she admitted it was “painful.”
Duterte said “the national sport of politicians is ‘plastikan’ (fakeness) so it is painful for me. For others, they are very good at it.”
No-el revival?
At yesterday’s press conference, Duterte said at least two members of the House of Representatives are allegedly pushing for a no-el (no election) scenario in 2028.
“Ask the media assigned at the House of Representatives. There are two congressmen pushing (for a no-el). I do not know how they would be able to rush it before 2028,” she said.

“They will take away the right of every citizen to select the president. They will put that power in a select group of elected officials and I think that is putting too much power to public officials, let us say oligarchs, that support their careers in government,” Duterte added.
While still waiting for the judgment of the Senate impeachment court, the Vice President said they have begun making preparations for the 2028 polls.
Last February, Duterte announced her plans to run for president.

She said they have started preparing their legal team and information and technology (IT) team because “it will be a fight against cheating and elections so initially we talked to election lawyers and some already committed to join the legal team for my campaign for president.”
Their IT team would be used to counter cheating since the elections would be automated.
As for their network on the ground, Duterte believed it is already “more or less stable” because they have been in place since the 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025 elections.
